environment.client_transport: bundled rusqlite, one embedded reader connection per concurrency slot, writes serialized through one shared writer connection, cached prepared statements, autocommit per statement

comparability.seed_policy: seed-{index}, tenant benchmark-tenant, index modulo seed count
comparability.document_policy: seed documents have id seed-{index}, name user-{index}, group index modulo 100, 256-byte payload
comparability.operation_policy: mixed uses index modulo 10: 0..4 read, 5..7 write, 8..9 query; read/query address index modulo seed count
comparability.write_id_policy: measured writes use measured-{global operation index}
comparability.durability_semantics: WAL journal with synchronous=NORMAL and a five-second busy timeout; autocommit statement acknowledgement
comparability.server_configuration_provenance: bundled sqlite at shipped defaults plus WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, busy_timeout=5000ms

limits: embedded reference: the measured member is this driver's own process, so the load generator and the database share one resource envelope

SQLite's concurrency model is many readers, one writer: reads and queries run concurrently on per-slot connections while every write serializes through one shared writer connection, the canonical deployment shape

sixteen contending per-slot writers instead busy-retry the WAL write lock and a starved slot can exceed the busy timeout; that retries SQLite's lock manager, not its storage, so this reference does not drive it
